title: NEMAR Zarr engine protocol (v0, unstable)
description: The header of one frame of the local protocol the NEMAR CLI engine speaks over stdin/stdout (frame: magic NZE0, u32 LE header_len, UTF-8 JSON header padded with spaces to an 8-byte boundary, then payload_bytes of binary samples; see ADR 0118). v0 is UNSTABLE and may change in place; the published versions that follow will not. The v0 engine speaks only protocol "0.1"; from v1 only the major must match. The engine reads a hello's protocol before validating the rest of it: a well-formed version it does not speak is unsupported_version whatever else the hello carries, and a malformed one is invalid_message. Missing data is never zeros: it is reported in filled_ranges (ADR 0005). Compatibility rule: every message is open. The engine MUST ignore unknown fields in a request and a client MUST ignore unknown fields in a response, so that from v1 a minor version may add fields in either direction; a known field with an invalid value is still invalid_message. Because a misspelled optional request field is ignored rather than refused, a client MUST check the answer against what it asked for: opened.representation, and a window's channels and dtype (dtype float64 means physical units, int16 digital). A field added to a request in a minor must be safe for an older engine to ignore, and a client relies on a newer request field only when the engine's hello response names a version that defines it.  JSON Schema alone cannot check the window payload_bytes arithmetic, that representation ids are unique, that opened.representation names one of them, that the bound representation is a zarr one whose sampling_frequency, nchans, ntimes, scale and offset are non-null, or that a representation's scale and offset have nchans entries; the zod mirror does, and a client in another language must check them itself. Closed lists and growth: a client treats an error code it does not know as internal; a client must refuse a window whose dtype, layout or byte_order it does not know, rather than guess at the bytes. Each message is one object, discriminated by type and, for hello and recipe, by its request-only field: a hello carrying client is a request and a hello response must not carry client; a recipe carrying handle is a request and a recipe response must not carry handle.

Id.description: Client-chosen request id; a response echoes the id of the request it answers.

PayloadBytesZero.description: payload_bytes is 0 on every message except window, and may be omitted (omitted means 0).

Handle.description: Opaque engine-chosen token naming an opened recording.

ChannelIndices.description: Zero-based channel indices into the representation the handle is bound to (0 to nchans - 1; an index of nchans or more is out_of_range). In a request, omitting channels means all channels of the bound representation in ascending order. In a window response, payload row i is channels[i]. Indices must not repeat.

ErrorCode.description: Why a request failed. A client treats a code it does not know as internal. A channel index of nchans or more is out_of_range; a representation id or recording the dataset does not have is not_found.

NeuroschemaRecord.description: The neuroschema record document (doc_type "record", https://github.com/nemarOrg/neuroschema) whose bids_relpath equals recording, passed through exactly as NEMAR publishes it in <dataset>/<version>/records.json for the dataset's latest published version, or null when none is available. It conforms to the neuroschema 0.4.x record schema, but its own schema_version stamp may be older (the published records say 0.3.0); do not reject it on the stamp. It describes the source file and is the authority for file-level facts: its signal_properties.sampling_frequency and signal_summary.nchans can differ from a representation's (a 500 Hz file is served as a 250 Hz Zarr group). It may come from a different dataset release than the representations, because records are published per version and the Zarr copy is the latest serving copy. Typed loosely here because neuroschema's own schemas do not have resolvable $id URLs; validate it with the neuroschema record schema if you need to. The engine never refuses to open because of it.

kind.description: What form the samples are stored in. v0 defines "zarr"; a client skips a kind it does not know.

id.description: Unique among this recording's representations; what open.representation names.

Representation.description: One form the recording's samples can be read from. Open like every response: an unknown kind, or an unknown field, is ignored by a client.

id.description: The Zarr group name, e.g. eeg_250hz.

store.description: The store's path relative to the dataset (Zarr index stores[].zarr).

modality.description: The group's modality (Zarr index group modality); one recording can hold groups of several modalities.

sampling_frequency.description: Hz, of this group (Zarr index group rate); null when the index has no positive rate. Field names follow neuroschema; values describe this group, not the source file.

source_sampling_frequency.description: Hz, the source rate the converter recorded for this group before its rate cap (Zarr index group source_rate_hz). For the file's own rate the record's signal_properties.sampling_frequency is the authority.

nchans.description: Channels in this group; null when the index has no channel count of at least 1.

ntimes.description: Samples per channel in this group; the time rule's out_of_range bound.

scale.description: Per channel (nchans entries; JSON Schema cannot check this, the zod mirror does and clients must). physical = digital * scale[c] + offset[c] for channel c; what a client reading units "digital" needs to convert. The engine fills scale and offset for the representation the handle is bound to and leaves them null for the others in v0 (neither schema copy checks that null). Channel names are deferred and not in v0.

offset.description: Per channel (nchans entries; not checkable in JSON Schema). See scale: physical = digital * scale[c] + offset[c].

protocol.description: The protocol version the client speaks, as MAJOR.MINOR.

HelloRequest.description: The client's opening message. The engine reads protocol before validating anything else in it: a well-formed version the engine does not speak is answered with unsupported_version even if the rest of the hello does not validate; unknown fields are ignored like in any request; a malformed protocol is invalid_message.

protocol.description: The protocol version the engine speaks; the client sends only what this version defines.

max_payload_bytes.description: The largest payload, in bytes, the engine will send in one window. A read_window whose window would exceed it is answered with too_large. The value is engine policy.

HelloResponse.description: Answers hello. It never carries client, the field that marks a hello request.

recording.description: The recording's BIDS path relative to the dataset repository root (neuroschema record bids_relpath, Zarr index stores[].path). The engine also accepts the store's zarr path.

representation.description: The id of the representation to bind the handle to. Omitted: the first zarr representation in the order opened lists them, which is the Zarr index's group order, as the MCP read_window tool picks the first group. In v0 only a zarr representation can be bound. An id the recording does not have, the id of a representation that is not zarr, or a recording with no zarr representation is not_found. A chosen zarr representation whose index entry has no positive rate, no channel count of at least 1 or no sample count is upstream_error: the serving index does not describe it well enough to read.

recording.description: Always the recording's BIDS path relative to the dataset repository root (Zarr index stores[].path), even when the request named the store's zarr path.

representation.description: The id of the representation the handle is bound to: read_window and recipe read it. It is always listed in representations, in v0 it is always a zarr representation, and its sampling_frequency, nchans, ntimes, scale and offset are non-null.

representations.description: Every representation of the recording, the bound one included, zarr ones in the Zarr index's group order. ids are unique.

Opened.description: Answers open. File-level metadata is in record (neuroschema); facts about each stored form are in representations, under neuroschema field names but describing that form.

units.description: Default physical (float64). digital is the raw int16 with no scale or offset applied.

ReadWindowRequest.description: Asks for the samples of a window of the representation the handle is bound to. Time rule, identical to the MCP read_window tool, with sampling_frequency and ntimes those of the representation the handle is bound to: start_sample = floor(start_s * sampling_frequency + 0.5) and n_samples = floor(duration_s * sampling_frequency + 0.5), with ties rounding up (shared/zarr/window-samples.ts). If n_samples < 1, or start_sample >= ntimes, or start_sample + n_samples > ntimes, the engine answers out_of_range; it never returns a truncated window.

filled_ranges.description: Sample ranges that could not be read: absolute sample indices of the recording (not offsets into the window), end-exclusive, sorted ascending, non-overlapping (adjacent ranges may or may not be merged), each inside [start_sample, start_sample + n_samples) of this window, with start_sample < end_sample. The payload values inside a filled range are the array's fill value (0 for these stores) converted like any other value, so for units "physical" they are offset[c], not zero; they are placeholders, never data (ADR 0005). Order, containment and start < end are guaranteed by the engine and are checked by neither schema copy.

payload_bytes.description: Required on window, even when 0. Must equal channels.length * n_samples * (8 for float64, 2 for int16). JSON Schema cannot express this arithmetic; the zod mirror and decodeFrame enforce it.

RecipeRequest.description: Asks for the read recipe of a window instead of its samples: the MCP read-recipe object that tells a client which store objects and byte ranges to fetch and decode to read the window itself. Nothing is read. Time rule, identical to the MCP read_window tool, with sampling_frequency and ntimes those of the representation the handle is bound to: start_sample = floor(start_s * sampling_frequency + 0.5) and n_samples = floor(duration_s * sampling_frequency + 0.5), with ties rounding up (shared/zarr/window-samples.ts). If n_samples < 1, or start_sample >= ntimes, or start_sample + n_samples > ntimes, the engine answers out_of_range; it never returns a truncated window.

recipe.description: The MCP read-recipe object (shared/contract/mcp.ts readRecipeSchema), typed loosely in v0. A full language-neutral recipe schema is deferred to v1.

RecipeResponse.description: Answers recipe. It never carries handle, the field that marks a recipe request.

id.description: The id of the request this answers. null only when the request's id could not be read (unparseable frame, invalid JSON, missing or non-integer id); every other message, and every request, carries an integer id of at least 1.
